status: source-reviewed executable procedures; no browser execution or pass claim
inventory_gate: Procedures preserve existing IDs, controls, modes, and dimensions. Execute only after the owning runner approves source inventory reconciliation and resource permit.
method_note: Current checked-in handlers use document.modelContext, awaited getTools(), and executeTool(registeredTool,input). The supplied documentary review was prepared against an older source shape; source references below describe this checkout and must be matched to the exact artifact SHA recorded by the runner. A/B routing evidence has two distinct mechanisms: the native fixture callback blocks after entry for output/side-effect checks; extension-origin calls are initiated by B's owned control signal causing A's real page to invoke a discovered extension tool while B is already active, with action approval also permitting a pre-handler focus switch. Read-only check/list claims use catalog-specific response evidence only.

preconditions: Run only after the owning runner approves inventory reconciliation and the resource permit. Record UTC time, Chrome version/channel, extension ID, source commit SHA, exact built artifact path plus SHA-256 and displayed version, profile identity, signed-in role, and the extension reload timestamp. Load that exact artifact in an owned disposable profile; confirm the side panel reports the same build identity. Repeat the build receipt after each full extension reload.

Use a secure-context page served from an origin you own (localhost is suitable), with a visible unique marker, a counter initialized to 0, and a read-only way to inspect both. In page DevTools, inspect the actual `document.modelContext` and method types. Do not polyfill or replace native objects. For documented local testing, use Chrome 149+ with `chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing` enabled and relaunch; Chrome 149 is the documented Origin Trial start, not a claim of general stable availability. Record the exact channel/build and flag state. If that flag or native API is absent, stop native-positive steps and mark them unresolved. If the actual native API is missing or incompatible, stop native-positive steps and record them unresolved; do not substitute a mock.

On owned secure-context localhost tab A, register one native page tool with a unique name and an object input schema requiring nonce:string. Its execute callback is a deterministic hold: set visible status to `entered:<nonce>` while keeping counter at 0; await a Promise resolved only by a `BroadcastChannel` message `{kind:'release',runId,nonce}`; after release increment A's counter exactly once and return `{nonce,counter:1,fixtureMarker:'webmcp-origin-A-<runId>'}`. Tab B is an owned same-origin control page with marker `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>`, counter 0, and its own distinct real native fixture registration `webmcp_fixture_B_<runId>` whose discovery metadata identifies B and whose callback is never invoked. B also has a Release A button that broadcasts the matching release and a Trigger A button for the extension-origin check below. Verify B's fixture with its own actual `await document.modelContext.getTools()` call. This control channel coordinates the fixture; it does not replace, wrap, or monkeypatch any native WebMCP object. Await actual `document.modelContext.registerTool({name,description,inputSchema,execute})` and independently verify the real native `await document.modelContext.getTools()` contains the tool once. Record exact code, method types, and signatures.

Use exact visible markers `webmcp-origin-A-<runId>` and `webmcp-origin-B-<runId>` and initialize both page counters to 0 for every run. Tab A's page tool is the only tool whose callback increments a counter. For manual Tools runs, focus the intended tab immediately before each run: ToolsView calls handler.run directly with assignedTabId:null and resolves whichever tab is focused. The held callback can prove the call's side effect/output stays on A after B is focused and releases it; it cannot prove when dispatcher target selection happened. Do not use that hold as evidence for read-only check/list, which never execute this callback. Manual runs do not prove dispatcher validation, admin gating, permissions, Ask/Act confirmation, or assigned-tab pinning.

For syntactically malformed text, use the Tools JSON editor and capture its `Invalid JSON` parser error before execution. For schema rejection, enter valid JSON with a wrong top-level type (for example `null`) and capture `Schema mismatch`; do not call either result a native API failure. For branch-level invalid values, use valid JSON that parses against the route schema and observe the handler's own structured result.

For the dispatcher lane, use a real agent invocation or real WebMCP page-to-extension call, record the exact authorized caller/role and permission state, and capture the actual gate or confirmation UI. Check one read-tier branch and the action-tier call branch separately. An admin positive proves no negative role gate. External action calls require confirmation in both Ask and Act modes; decline once and verify no page side effect. Keep the feature-test procedure and inventory cell unexecuted until this run occurs.

For the held page-tool call path, only use an exact tool that is actually advertised to the signed-in admin in the current request; if no live agent route exists, leave dispatcher tab-routing unresolved and retain the manual handler case. Start a real dispatcher action with Ask mode enabled while A is the assigned tab; wait until its actual approval card appears (handler has not run yet), focus B and confirm B is active, then approve. Require A status `entered:<nonce>` with counters still A=0/B=0; press B's Release A button; require returned fixtureMarker A, A counter=1, B counter=0. This forces focus to B before handler target resolution and release after entry. Also run a direct manual call from A, wait for entered, switch to B, release from B, and require the same A-only result, labeling it handler behavior only. For extension-origin routing, require real extension registrations on A. While B is already active, press B's Trigger A button; A's own page script then invokes the discovered real `matrx.webmcp_list_page_tools` or `matrx.chrome_webmcp` RegisteredTool through native `document.modelContext.executeTool`. For check/list, require the A response to include `webmcp_fixture_A_<runId>` and exclude `webmcp_fixture_B_<runId>`, while B's independent native catalog shows the inverse; do not claim the fixture callback hold tested those read-only branches. For the action call, keep B active through the approval card, approve, then use B's Release A button and require the side effect only on A. For closed-origin checks, distinguish a request whose sender tab is already closed before delivery (`webmcp: origin tab unavailable`) from A closed after a real action approval is pending (explicit no-active-tab/closed-tab failure, no effect on B). Never infer a negative gate from an admin positive.

After page reload, the owned page script registers again and repeats native discovery/call with fresh runId, nonce, counters, and A/B markers. Fully reload the exact extension artifact, verify ID/version/path and a fresh build receipt, reload pages, and let the extension register again. For the audit receipt, ensure the disposable profile contains only owned fixture tabs across all windows and that the active browser window contains only A and B. On A, inspect the real catalog, find `matrx.list_open_tabs`, and execute the discovered RegisteredTool with `{all_windows:false,url:'http://localhost:<PORT>/webmcp-fixture/*'}` (the current handler schema supports both fields). Capture only the extension audit receipt fields `origin=webmcp`, call/tool identity, completion outcome, and timestamp; redact the returned tab array, URLs, titles, IDs, and query strings. Record the profile/tab hygiene check without retaining unrelated browsing data. Manual Tools runs are not WebMCP receipts. Cleanup by unregistering only if the native API supports it; otherwise close the owned profile/pages and verify no fixture tab or owned registration remains.
steps: On focused fixture tab A, record `await document.modelContext.getTools()` and its count. In Tools > Catalog > All handlers, run `webmcp_check_availability` with `{}`. Require `available:true` and `tool_count` equal to the awaited native catalog length. Repeat once after registering the unique fixture tool and verify the count increases by one. Save the independent DevTools observation and handler output together.
Run the malformed-text and valid-JSON-wrong-top-level-type checks described above. Record parser/schema errors as local input validation outcomes; neither should invoke the page API.

Attempt a no-native-API case only on an actual browser/page context where direct inspection proves `document.modelContext.getTools` is absent; do not delete or shadow the native property. If no such genuine context exists, record unavailable branch not exercised. Attempt a restricted browser tab only if one is available; record the Chrome scripting rejection separately from WebMCP unavailable. Also run with no selected tab if the real Tools UI can produce that state, expecting `No active tab`.

Perform the separate dispatcher lane for this read-tier, admin-only handler: verify exact advertised availability for the admin before invocation, then use an authorized member profile/call to verify the actual admin rejection. Do not infer member denial from the admin success or the manual badge. Use the common precondition's pending approval to switch to B before the action handler starts; use its separate B-triggered native invocation to prove extension-origin sender A while B is already active. Keep read-only check/list evidence separate from the held callback.
Complete the page reload and full extension reload sequence in the common preconditions; retain pre/post build receipts, direct native catalog observations, outputs, tab markers, and cleanup result.
expected: A valid native positive requires observed real `document.modelContext.getTools`, an awaited catalog, and `available:true` with matching length. If native detection or the result differs, capture the exact shape/error and leave positive unresolved; no polyfill or guessed browser-version explanation counts.

No-tab and Chrome scripting failures are bounded handler errors. A native API absence is only established by direct observation on that exact page/build. Manual output demonstrates handler execution only; role, advertisement, permission and assigned-tab claims require the separate dispatcher evidence. The read-only dispatcher route is covered only by the separate B-triggered invocation from A while B is already active, with distinct A/B native catalog evidence.
For admin/member distinction, an admin positive does not prove the member gate. Capture actual dispatcher result and preserve no-run/no-side-effect evidence for a denied member call.
limits: The procedure is a plan, not an observation. It does not claim any Chrome build exposes the API.

Require `ok:true`, returned nonce/fixture marker, returned counter N+1, and independent visible counter N+1. Verify tab B marker and counter are unchanged.

Run `{"name":"unknown-<unique suffix>","arguments":{}}` and require `ok:false` with not-found reason and unchanged counter. Run valid outer JSON with `arguments:null`, a string, an array, and an object with a deliberately invalid fixture field; record handler/native errors separately. The handler itself rejects non-object arguments before calling `executeTool`; only the fixture's own schema execution demonstrates its schema response.

Submit missing/empty name as valid JSON and capture schema mismatch; malformed JSON must produce parser error. On actual API-absent page, capture `WebMCP unavailable`; on restricted tab capture Chrome scripting error. Do not fabricate API absence or interpret these as permission denials.

Test Ask and Act: external page-origin calls still require user confirmation in both; decline and verify counter unchanged, then approve one fresh nonce and verify exactly one increment. Confirm optional Chrome permission state and any permission denial separately from confirmation UI. Run A-to-B switch and closed-A checks from common preconditions.

After page reload, register again, establish a new N, and repeat once. Fully reload the exact extension artifact, refresh build receipt, reload/re-register page, and repeat with fresh nonce. Capture the actual external `origin=webmcp` resource receipt and clean up.
expected: A native positive requires discovered RegisteredTool passed to the current handler's `executeTool(tool, input)` path, returned nonce/marker, and independent one-step visible side effect. An API mock, handler-only fabricated result, or return value without counter readback is not a positive. During the held run, capture entry with both counters still 0, B active before release, then response marker A and final counts A=1/B=0.
